cases.title: Lint only the changed packages in the Stop hook
cases.head: fb6695d44accefdeb5baf47793b8adca883dec7d

expect.finding: --enable-only also empties the formatter config, so golangci-lint run --fix formats its fixes with no goimports, gci or golines: a fix can leave an unused import (the build fails) or a line over the limit, and the hook still exits 0.

The stamp can record a state that was never linted: untracked files are hashed by content only (git hash-object --stdin-paths), so moving or renaming one keeps the hash; or the stamp is computed after the run, so an edit made during the run is stamped as linted.
The file-name allowlist [[:alnum:]_./+~-] under LC_ALL=C rejects a valid non-ASCII file name (a/café.go), so that file is not formatted.
The sed that parses the linter list keeps only [a-z0-9-]*, so a linter whose name holds '_' (wsl_v5, gomodguard_v2) is dropped from the hook.

The PR body says a broken caller in a package that imports a changed package is a compile error; many findings in an importer compile fine (errcheck on a new error result, an incomplete exhaustive switch, a lock copied by value).

cases.title: Print Go test results through gotestsum
cases.head: cf048fdde48fe2640aaf494b5c2593bb9fb81922

expect.finding: make test prints only the output go test -json assigns to the failed test: TestMain output (before or after m.Run, such as a goroutine-leak report) and output of passing tests are no longer printed, and no copy of the full output is kept.
With --stream the text-log decoder runs in a process substitution >(...), whose exit status pipefail does not see: a decoder failure no longer fails the shard.
The PR description is wrong about make test-rerun: a test that fails then passes on rerun gets no (re-run N) label in that place, and the target exits 0.

cases.title: Stop StraightLineDistances from queuing a cell more than once
cases.head: bfe828339c68509a04fa84a9ed4ae86764623528

expect.finding: No test pins that each cell is queued once: an edit that appends a cell again when it already holds the current distance (d == distance) leaves every test green.

The enqueueStraightLineCandidates docstring says the scan goes up to the first obstacle; it also ends at the grid edge, at the start and at a cell of an earlier level, and passes over a cell of the same level.
The full go vet suite no longer runs on the generated files (*/db/generated/): generated: lax drops golangci-lint findings there, and the shards' compile step runs only the go test vet subset.
.golangci.yml excludes gosec G104 and G301/G302/G307, which gosec.includes does not enable: dead rules that read as policy.

A comment does not match the code: scripts/integration-tests.sh says a split shard's run filter repeats the skip filter of the shard it came from (false for the metascheduler shards), or ci-validation.yml says the step compiles the test binaries and saves them (go test does not cache its link step).

cases.title: [sc-5162] Stamp appended restocking line item versions after the version they supersede
cases.head: 01408e886e58176cee8ddc70ef4dd7ef3af0850c

expect.finding: Two concurrent appenders now compute the same MAX(created_at) + 1 µs, so their rows are identical and PostgreSQL reports the primary key, which handleVersionInsertError does not retry; handlePickVersionInsertError retries every unique violation.

The SQL comment on the insert query claims more than the code: the inversion needs a version stamped (not only committed) after this transaction's BEGIN, or version 1 is stamped by the writing process only for line items created with their manifest.
The PR body says every latest-version read orders by created_at DESC, version DESC; GetRestockingLineItemsForUpdate takes MAX(version).

cases.title: [sc-5159] Settle a completed restock operation so its duplicate resume is consumed
cases.head: 79858597fdf6f3bb0d84678db880df76d4d4328c

expect.finding: ResolvedRestockResumes holds one operation per Lifty, and two paths clear it without settling the operation (a second inventory resolution overwrites it; reportUnmatchedSuccessSignal consumes it), so a later resume that names the first operation ends the Lifty's current work.
A resume that names an unknown operation falls to the default branch and ends the Lifty's current work with no Warn or Error log.

cases.title: [sc-5169] Skip a carried tote whose carrier is held in place
cases.head: aecec40a9ee3ec94bac5fe843d1f8628a988bd15

expect.finding: Dropping the unassigned subset of a tote a Maintenance Lifty carries can remove the order from ls.Orders; a RequestPick directive then fails with 'unknown order' (orderByID), which is not ErrDirectiveInfeasible, so the run fails and a SYSTEM_STOP is published.

TestReconcileJudgesACarriedToteByItsCarrier uses a tote that is both carried by pepe and stacked in at Z=1, a state the world cannot reach, so the test passes even when the carried-tote rule is removed.

cases.title: [sc-4954] Keep a command result that arrives before the plan loop waits for it
cases.head: 7ede7e9c69d0023b9e8583b9ce46ec18789d6633

expect.finding: With TMPLT_AC_HANDLE_ACK_ASYNC on, a later command whose acknowledgement and result are both buffered: the loop reads the result and removes the entry before the acknowledgement goroutine calls GetAckChannel, which fails and publishes a system stop for a command that succeeded. The tests force async acknowledgements off.

AddAfterExecutionCallback or AddAfterFailureCallback on an execution that is already signalled returns nil and the callback never runs; at the merge base the call returned ErrExecutionNotFound, which callers escalate to a system stop.
An early report of command N+1 is recorded under the command the loop still waits on (agentState.CommandID/CommandType): wrong history entry and wrong commands_executed message.
Timeout and context-cancel exits rely on cleanupRemainingCommandChannels(index) to remove the signalled entry; changing those calls to index+1 passes every test.
A cmdExecuted test reads from a closed channel and gets a zero result with Success == false, so it passes on the merge base too.

cases.title: [sc-5193] Stop the preflight tests from crashing when they run more than once
cases.head: b42a83e85ee2edddc794c134b9c4df80145224b0

expect.finding: The preflight main_test.go comment claims sync.Pool reuses an entry only on the P that put it back and that one P makes the reuse certain; Get steals from other Ps through getSlow, and under -race Put drops a quarter of the entries.
The DisableDeadlockTimerPool docstring tells callers how to use it ('Call it in the TestMain of a package that ...'), which CLAUDE.md keeps out of docstrings.
